internal.title: SEV1 Incident: Checkout Service Error Rate Spike Due to Payment Service Error Injection
internal.body:
At 10:20 UTC, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Diagnosis identified the root cause as an error injection in the payment service, specifically due to an active 'paymentFailure' flag causing 100% error rate with 'Invalid token' errors. The cart service was ruled out as a fault source due to negligible error rates.

The remediation action was to disable the 'paymentFailure' flag at 10:40 UTC, which was approved and executed promptly. Post-action monitoring confirmed recovery with error rates returning to normal levels.

Timeline:
- 10:20:33: Alert received for checkout service error rate spike.
- 10:40:16: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection.
- 10:40:22: Flag disabling proposed, approved, and executed.
- 10:40:22: Recovery verified with normalized error rates.

This incident highlights the impact of error injection flags on dependent services and the importance of rapid diagnosis and flag management.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing issues
external.body: Between 10:20 and 10:40 UTC, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to payment processing errors. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a configuration causing payment failures. Normal service has been restored and customers should no longer experience checkout problems.
